course_description:
Building upon your understanding of how students learn, this course aims to focus on your teaching practice in your context. This course aims to develop your knowledge, comprehension and application of skills in curriculum and assessment design and selection of pedagogies most appropriate to your discipline area. Drawing on knowledge from self-directed learning, you will apply theory to practice in the workshops in the context of UQ policies, educational technologies, and educational priorities. You will work collaboratively to identify potential areas in your course curriculum, assessment and pedagogy and your teaching practice that you might enhance. You will examine, reflect on and justify the use of curriculum design principles in relation to your own practice and that of others. The course offers an opportunity to select areas of practice that are most appropriate for your context or personal development. You will need a curriculum offering – such as a course, module, or professional development activity – that you can work on and develop throughout the course. This could be a new curriculum offering or redesign of an existing one, or an approved hypothetical scenario for development.

In addition to course credit, successful completion of Curriculum Design at UQ (EDHE6002) and Teaching in Practice (EDHE6003) within three years can also lead to conferral of HEA Fellowship, subject to external moderation.

course_aims: This course aims to develop participants' knowledge, comprehension and application of skills in curriculum and assessment design and selection of pedagogies most appropriate to the participant's discipline area and areas of interest. The course is tailored to participant's unique teaching and learning environments to enhance student learning experiences, advance their academic career and evidence their impact. The course is intended to encourage participants to adopt scholarly approach to their teaching, recognising the breadth of characteristics involved in the development of teaching expertise in higher education across all career stages.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically evaluate curriculum, assessment and pedagogic practice in light of how students learn in specific higher education contexts
Design engaging and inclusive learning activities and assessment
Evaluate and enhance personal teaching practice
Collaborate with members of a community of practice in teaching and learning at UQ.

assessment_details.task_description: The Showcase and Reflection assessment provides you with a collaborative opportunity to articulate, evaluate, and refine your curriculum (re)design through peer discussion, feedback, and critical reflection. This assessment has two parts: Part 1: Showcase Presentation (20minutes). Share and justify your curriculum (re)design with peers, receive formative feedback, and engage in reflective discussion to inform your final presentation. Part 2: Showcase Reflection (approximately 500 words). Reflect on your Showcase experience, summarise peer feedback, identify improvements to your design, and consider what you’ve learned from others’ presentations. learning_activities.topic: Workshop 1: Curriculum design for learning In this workshop, we will cover course aims, assessment and activities organisation, the principles and practice of backwards design, the importance of context, and compelling questions for curriculum development. We will also focus on learners and their learning and how you can set the scene for your learners. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Workshop 2: Designing Learning In this workshop, we will explore developing and aligning quality learning outcomes and assessment principles. You will also have time to work on Assessment 1 Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Workshop 3: Assessing learning In this workshop we will explore assessment in practice, drawing on principles of constructive alignment. We focus on assessment design, grading, rubrics, and feedback as well as the limits and opportunities of AI with regards to assessment. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Workshop 4: Pedagogy In this workshop, you will discuss and apply pedagogical principles and apply pedagogical principles in practice. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Workshop 5: Bringing it all together In this workshop, you will bring together all the learning from the course and prepare your design with support Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Showcase Presentation and Reflection In this Showcase, you will present your curriculum (re-)design and engage in peer feedback conversations. Attendance is mandatory. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
